types.name: Serious seeker
types.persona: You are {age} and you want a steady relationship, so you would pay for this app if the people on it feel real and close to you.

types.name: Tired of swiping
types.persona: You are {age} and you have used other dating apps for a long time with little luck, so you doubt big promises and you do not want to pay again too soon.

types.name: Curious first timer
types.persona: You are {age} and you have never really tried dating this way, so a new app feels exciting to you but you want to try it for free and learn how it works first.

types.name: Casual and bored
types.persona: You are {age} and you are not looking for anything serious right now, so you swipe when you are bored and you would not pay to keep going.

types.name: Busy and picky
types.persona: You are {age} and you have very little free time, so you like getting only a few choices a day if they are good ones and you can pay a small weekly price to save time.

types.name: Hopeful but short on cash
types.persona: You are {age} and you would love to meet someone soon, but you watch every dollar so a weekly price makes you think hard before you pay.

types.name: Careful about trust
types.persona: You are {age} and you worry that some people may not be who they say they are, so you read reviews and you wait for proof that people are real before you pay.

types.name: Trying again
types.persona: You are {age} and you took a break after a past relationship, so you feel ready again and a brand new app makes you hopeful that this time could be different.

rationale: These eight types cover the main ways single people aged 18 to 34 in the United States react when a new dating app asks for money, from strong hope for a real relationship to casual use with no wish to pay. The biggest shares go to people who have swiped before with little luck, people who are casual, and people who are curious, because a new app mostly draws trial and hope at first rather than sure payers on day one. Smaller shares go to careful people and people trying again, who are fewer but may stay longer if early matches feel close and real. The mix gives weight to price, trust, free time, and how much each person wants a relationship, which are the points where the two launch plans differ most.
